prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S090: The Baggage Operations Supervisor sets local congestion thresholds and confirms the authorized response to sustained overload.
S091: Tern is the operational alias used for the Baggage Operations Supervisor in sortation coordination.
S092: When a planned lane is unavailable, the Baggage Control System selects an approved alternate route only if screening status and flight timing remain valid.
S093: Bags with an unresolved destination or a route outside their handling limits are diverted to the Secondary Inspection Chute.
S094: The Image Resolution Desk resolves image-related holds before affected bags are returned to normal sortation.
S095: The Explosives Response Team manages security holds under the applicable response procedures.
S096: A bag returns to normal handling only after its identity, examination outcome, and routing authorization agree.
S097: The East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor are selected according to the active plan and available capacity.
S098: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit operates within its assigned flight window and reports when its usable capacity is constrained.
S099: The Transfer Bag Feeder continues to hold transfer bags until screening status and intended onward handling are confirmed.
S100: The Bag Reconciliation Station compares bag identity with the active handling record and flags unresolved discrepancies.
S101: The Bag Reconciliation Station sends a Bag Match Query when bag identity cannot be reconciled with the active handling record.
S102: Bags found on a stopped or misdirected path are held from onward movement until their location and identity are established.
S103: The Maintenance Technician isolates a failed conveyor section and confirms that the route is safe before service resumes.
S104: The Baggage Operations Supervisor authorizes recovery to the approved sort plan after the cause of the abnormal path has been addressed.
S105: Flight Data Gateway maintains scheduled flight identifiers, destinations, planned departure times, and revisions needed for baggage planning.
S106: Flight schedules include airline-specific dispatch targets and connection windows, and changes are time-stamped for operational use.
S107: Baggage Control System evaluates flight assignments against current schedule data before accepting bag routing instructions.
S108: The planned dispatch time is the reference for prioritizing bags, while the published departure time remains the passenger-facing schedule value.
S109: Baggage Control System applies cutoff profiles configured for each carrier, flight, and operating condition.
S110: A bag accepted before cutoff retains its assigned flight unless a subsequent schedule or operational change requires reassessment.
S111: When schedule revisions move a departure earlier, Baggage Operations Supervisor reviews affected flights and directs priority adjustments.
S112: Cutoff values account for screening, sortation, make-up, and transfer handling allowances rather than only aircraft departure.
S113: Baggage Control System receives the Flight Cutoff Advisory.
S114: Baggage Control System compares remaining processing time with route-specific handling estimates.
S115: Bags with confirmed screening clearance may proceed to flight-specific sort destinations when capacity is available.
S116: Bags awaiting screening are held from final flight induction even when their scheduled departure is near.
S117: North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner record screening outcomes for inducted bags.
S118: The Image Resolution Desk reviews unresolved images, and final routing remains withheld until disposition is recorded.
S119: A positive threat indication suspends ordinary routing until the authorized security disposition is entered.
S120: Explosives Response Team produces the Custody Seal Log.
S121: When screening disposition is pending, Baggage Control System preserves a recoverable bag-to-flight association rather than releasing the bag to make-up.
S122: Primary Crossbelt Sorter routes eligible bags according to flight assignment and current cutoff priority.
S123: Concourse Zone Controller coordinates induction demand with available conveyor capacity across the operating area.
S124: Induction Tray Conveyor admits bags in priority order, subject to scan confirmation and safe spacing.
S125: East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor receive flight groups according to active allocation rules.
S126: Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit presents bags for outbound loading only after flight grouping and screening status are confirmed.
S127: Outbound Load Control Desk uses planned dispatch time and load-close targets to monitor whether assigned bags can be accepted.
S128: Airline Ramp Coordinator reports changes to loading readiness that could alter the usable cutoff.
S129: Baggage Operations Supervisor may defer lower-priority bags when a flight's remaining processing window is insufficient.
S130: Bags missing the active flight cutoff are held for reassignment or recovery rather than routed into an unavailable departure build.
S131: Make-up allocation begins when the active flight assignment and available build positions are confirmed.
S132: Baggage Operations Supervisor authorizes release to a make-up position only when the flight remains within its processing window.
S133: Flight Data Gateway maintains the flight identity and departure timing used for make-up planning.
S134: Mosslight assigns bags to active make-up lanes using current zone status.
S135: Velvet records each bag's screening disposition and release state against its flight assignment.
